newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Marieberg to move shares to avoid tax.
newsitem.headline: Marieberg to move shares to avoid tax.

text.p: Swedish newspaper publisher Marieberg said on Monday it had joined the list of companies applying to move its shares from the Stockholm bourse main A list to the smaller O list to avoid a new tax law.
Marieberg, which is owned by the Bonnier family, said its last day of trading on the A list would be June 13 and it would trade on the O list from June 16.
Family-controlled Swedish companies are lining up to leave the A list and head for the smaller O list as a new law approved by parliament last week forces their owners to pay higher wealth tax.
Swedish business paper Dagens Industri calculated that by moving its Marieberg shares to the O-list, the Bonnier family can save more than 11 million crowns in taxes a year.

A new law that took effect in late 1996 forces Swedes with wealth exceeding 900,000 crowns to pay 1.5 percent tax on 100 percent of the value of shares listed on the A list, up from 75 percent, while shares on the O list remain exempt from tax.
A list of companies are fleeing the A list including fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, construction group Lundbergs and investment company Latour.
Hennes & Mauritz shares plunged on the transfer announcement last week as some institutional investors have internal rules saying they can only invest in shares on the A list.
Marieberg announced the planned transfer after the Stockholm Stock Exchange's close on Monday. Its share ended at 199 crowns, down eight.
